subject: Subprocessor acceptance & evidence checklist
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightline-pay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Security <security@brightline-pay.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: consolidated subprocessor list + evidence for DPA review

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As part of our legal & security intake we need a consolidated list of Redwood's subprocessors that will potentially process Brightline customer data for the scope of the current pilot. Specifically we need: 

- A CSV with name, role (hosting, telemetry, analytics, KMS, CDN), country of processing, encryption jurisdiction, and whether data transfers outside of US occur.
- Any recent attestations or SOC/Security summary for onshore/on-prem fallbacks.
- A short note on whether any telemetry or observability partners retain request/response payloads beyond 30 days.

Can you provide this by EOD Tuesday PST? If there are any subprocessors that require temporary access (e.g., support windows), please flag those and include planned mitigation (onshore fallback, escrow, encryption-in-flight).

We may need a signed addendum depending on findings — happy to share a template.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Integrations, Brightline Payments
Attachments: none
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: consolidated subprocessor list + evidence for DPA review

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Brightline's list request. They want a CSV and supporting evidence by EOD Tuesday PST (that's 2027-06-22).

Quick asks:
- Marissa: can you assemble the subprocessor matrix and call out any partners with cross-border exports? Make sure to include encryption jurisdiction column.
- Ben: can you confirm KMS/HSM locations and whether we can add an onshore fallback note for any transit partners? If any telemetry partner retains payload >30 days, flag it.

I'll handle the outreach on our side and send the signed DPA template if they request it. If we need legal/ops to sign any addendum, I'll escalate.

Thanks —
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: consolidated subprocessor list + evidence for DPA review

Jordan / Ben — putting the attached matrix together now. Notes below: 

- Matrix attached: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20270621.csv (columns: vendor, role, country, data_types, encryption_jurisdiction, retention_days, onshore_fallback_available)
- Export path diagram attached: export_path_diagram.png (high level: requests -> edge proxy -> runtime -> telemetry relay -> analytics).
- KMS/HSM: Ben confirms primary KMS in us-east-1 (AWS KMS) and on-prem HSM in our EU private deployment for customers who require it. For Brightline pilot (US-only) the primary KMS jurisdiction is US.
- Telemetry retention: By default observability/metrics traces retain up to 90 days; request/response payload capture is disabled for hosted accounts. We do have temporary support windows (max 7 days) for reproducing customer issues; those are flagged in the matrix with planned deletion notes.
- Temporary access: none planned for the pilot; if a vendor requires temporary access we'll require an access window + RBAC + onshore session recording.

I also prepared a short cover note to attach to the DPA addendum if Legal asks for one. Draft DocuSign envelope is available (link below) but Legal needs to sign the addendum first.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20270621.csv (CSV), export_path_diagram.png (PNG)
Related link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Brightline/Subprocessor-Matrix-20270621
DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/envelopes/EB-998172

Will finalize CSV with Ben's KMS entries once he confirms the HSM export jurisdiction.

—Marissa
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@brightline-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Brightline Security <security@brightline-pay.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated subprocessor list + evidence for DPA review

Hi Laura — thanks for the note and the clear checklist. Please find attached the consolidated matrix and a short export-path diagram. Key points up front: 

- Attached matrix: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20270621.csv (includes role, country, encryption jurisdiction, retention, and any temporary access flags).
- Export path diagram attached for quick mapping.
- KMS: Primary KMS is AWS KMS (us-east-1). We also support customer-managed HSM for Private deployments; not used in the pilot.
- Telemetry: default instrumentation does not capture customer request/response payloads for our hosted API; traces and metrics retained for up to 90 days. Any short-lived support captures are flagged in the matrix and are auto-deleted per our retention policy (max 7 days).

If Brightline requires an addendum we can sign a DPA annex; we have a prepared draft waiting on Legal to execute. DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/envelopes/EB-998172

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether the CSV answers your immediate needs or whether legal needs deeper evidence (SOC summary, encryption attestation).
2) If you want the DPA annexed, confirm signatories and we’ll route to Redwood Legal.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
